sources.text:
The Hay Market Square (Polish: Rynek Sienny; German: Heumarkt) is an urban square in Szczecin, Poland. It is located between Sienna and Księcia Mściwoja II Streets, within the Old Town neighbourhood of the Downtown district. It was developed in the Middle Ages as a market place. One of buildings neighbouring it is the Old Town Hall, dating to the 15th century.


== History ==
The market place was developed in the Middle Ages. In 1310, its name was recorded in Latin as forum antiquum, meaning the Old Market Place, and after 1325, it began being referred to as the Hay Market Square, after the hay being one of the products sold there.
In the 15th century, at its corner was constructed the Old Town Hall with Gothic architecture, in place of the previous wooden building. In the 17th century, it was rebuilt in the Baroque style.
In 1835, at the western end of the square was opened the stock exchange building, replacing the sailor accommodations.
In 1879, the Old Town Hall ceased to house the municipal government, with its spaces being rented to private businesses. In the late 19th century, around the square were constructed tenement houses, mostly designed in the Baroque style, later refurbished...
